rv.q: The beautifully crafted and disorienting play Right Now now on at Humboldt Park’s Facility Theatre is the kind of storefront theater that makes Chicago second to none for mind altering drama.
You might need to take time to mull over what you've seen, but you will have no doubt whatsoever that it was something provocative and fascinating.
This handsome and cunning production offers a slice of psychological absurdity.

This is an excellent play that is very much worth seeing, despite some overly familiar tropes (including a disturbing sound effect that’s practically identical to one I saw in another play I just reviewed called The Writer) and some derivative themes concerning grief and trauma.

cn.t: Critics praise this dreamlike, disorienting thriller for its riveting direction and exquisite craft, drawing comparisons to Pinter and "Rosemary's Baby" while delivering mind-altering storefront drama.
